'''Hamed Ehdadi Haddadi''' ({{langx|fa|حامد حدادی}}, {{IPA|fa|hɑmɛd ɛ hæddɑdi}}, born May 19, 1985) is an Iranian professional [[basketball]] player for (Esteghlal BC) of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League]] (IBSL). He played at the [[Centre (basketball)|center]] position and is {{convert|7|ft|2|in|m|abbr=in|sp=us}} tall and weighs {{convert|254|lb|kg|abbr=off|sp=us}}. Haddadi was the first [[Iranian peoples|Iranian]] to play in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) when he debuted with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Michaela |last1=Yisrael |first2=Richard |last2=Roth |url=http://www.cnn.com/2010/SPORT/04/14/iranian.basketball.player/index.html |title=Iranian playing in NBA scores with America |publisher=Cnn.com |access-date=2014-06-13}}</ref> He played with the Grizzlies until 2013 before bouncing around the league with the [[Phoenix Suns]]. In 2013, he returned home to Iran before playing in China.

==Professional career==
===Iran===
Before officially playing for a professional Iranian team, Haddadi started his basketball stint with a hometown team of his known as [[Shahin Ahvaz F.C.|Shahin Ahvaz]]. His stint there would ultimately allow Haddadi to play in the [[Iranian Basketball Super League]] with [[Paykan Tehran]] and [[Saba Battery Tehran BC|Saba Battery]]. In 2004, Haddadi would also play for [[Sanam Tehran]] for a bit as well. In August 2007, while still playing in Iran, he rejected a contract offer from the [[Naša Sinalko Liga|Serbian League]] team [[KK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]] in order to play for Saba Battery.<ref>{{cite news |title=IRI – Remedial Tonic takes Iran's basketball to Beijing |url=http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/news/lateNews/fibaEven/olymMen/p/newsid/24692/arti.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080910083903/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/news/lateNews/fibaEven/olymMen/p/newsid/24692/arti.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 10, 2008 |publisher=[[FIBA]] |date=May 13, 2008 |access-date=2008-05-13}}</ref>

During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Haddadi signed a short-term contract with his hometown team, [[Melli Haffari Ahvaz BC|Melli Haffari Ahvaz]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120903215846/http://www.mehrnews.com/en/NewsDetail.aspx?NewsID=1437043|title=Hamed Haddadi joins Melli Haffari}}</ref> During this period Haddadi received no salary from the team.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pfdctv.com/?p=8497 |title=Interview with Hamed Haddadi – 5/18/2013 |publisher=Pfdctv.com |date=2013-05-18 |access-date=2014-06-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150107122247/http://www.pfdctv.com/?p=8497 |archive-date=2015-01-07 |url-status=usurped }}</ref>

During the 2013 offseason, Haddadi signed a short-term contract with [[Foolad Mahan Isfahan BC|Foolad Mahan Isfahan]]. After his first stint with the [[Chinese Basketball Association]], Haddadi would return to Iran once again to play for [[Mahram Tehran BC|Mahram Tehran]] to play out the rest of their season.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

On March 9, 2016, Haddadi signed with [[Petrochimi Bandar Imam BC|Petrochimi Bandar Imam]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League|Iranian Super League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Petrochimi signs Hamed Haddadi and Ivan Johnson|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/193592/petrochimi-signs-hamed-haddadi-and-ivan-johnson.html|work=Sportando.com|date=March 9, 2016|access-date=March 12, 2016}}</ref> However, he wouldn't make his debut until later on in March due to his CBA Finals duties with the [[Sichuan Blue Whales]] at the time. He would return to that same team once again after the [[2016-17 CBA season]] concluded for Sichuan. This time around, however, he would play for them for the entirety of the 2017–18 season.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

On December 14, 2025, Haddadi signed with '''Esteghlal BC''' of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League]] (IBSL).<ref>{{cite web |title=Haddadi comes back to Naft Abadan |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Iran/news/846369/Haddadi-comes-back-to-Naft-Abadan |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=22 October 2024 |date=5 January 2024}}</ref>

===United Arab Emirates===
In 2003, Haddadi was assigned by Paykan Tehran to play for [[Al-Nasr SC (Dubai)|Al-Nasr]] from [[Dubai]] in the [[United Arab Emirates]] for a short period of time. He would ultimately return with Paykan after his stint with Al-Nasr.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

===NBA career===
====Memphis Grizzlies====
Before the [[2004 NBA draft]], Haddadi declared himself [[Eligibility for the NBA Draft|eligible for the draft]] as an early entrant.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2004/early_040618.html |title=Fifty-Three Early Entry Candidates Withdraw |work=Nba.com |access-date=2014-06-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020181612/http://www.nba.com/draft2004/early_040618.html |archive-date=2012-10-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref> However, he went [[Undrafted sportsperson|undrafted]] in the draft and therefore became a free agent.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

Haddadi received offers from NBA teams prior to the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics|2008 Summer Olympics]] and stated he would sign with a team after the games. Complications existed because of legal restrictions regarding business dealings between U.S. companies and Iranian citizens.<ref>Adrian Wojnarowski, [https://sports.yahoo.com/olympics/beijing/basketball/news?slug=aw-nbairan081608 NBA teams seek clearance to sign Iranian], August 16, 2008</ref><ref>[http://www.interbasket.net/news/437/2008/08/20/nba-cleared-to-talk-deal-with-hamed-ehadadi NBA cleared to talk, deal with Hamed Haddadi] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090814191543/http://www.interbasket.net/news/437/2008/08/20/nba-cleared-to-talk-deal-with-hamed-ehadadi/ |date=2009-08-14 }}, August 20, 2008</ref>

On August 28, 2008, Haddadi signed with the [[NBA]]'s [[Memphis Grizzlies]] as a free-agent. Haddadi scored four points in 17 minutes of action in his first NBA preseason game, an October 7, 2008 loss at the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_sign_hamed_haddadi-080828.html |title=Grizzlies sign Iranian centre Hamed Haddadi | THE OFFICIAL SITE OF THE MEMPHIS GRIZZLIES |work=Nba.com |access-date=2014-06-13}}</ref><ref>[http://www.tehrantimes.com/index_View.asp?code=175647 Hamed Haddadi hits out at NBA legal counsel], August 19, 2008</ref>

Haddadi averaged 1.7 points and 3.3 rebounds in 9.7 minutes in six preseason games with the Grizzlies, and made his regular season debut on December 30, when he played 4 minutes in a loss against the [[Phoenix Suns]], hitting both of his [[free throw]]s and grabbing one rebound.<ref name="debut">{{cite web |url=http://www.rotoworld.com/content/playerpages/playerbreakingnews.asp?sport=NBA&id=1561&line=106814&spln=1 |title=Grizzlies rookie Haddadi makes NBA debut |publisher=Rotoworld.com |access-date=2014-06-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090207195020/http://www.rotoworld.com/content/playerpages/playerbreakingnews.asp?sport=NBA&id=1561&line=106814&spln=1 |archive-date=2009-02-07 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=FedExForum, Memphis, TN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=281230029 |title=Suns 101, Grizzlies 89 – Box score |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2008-12-30 |access-date=2014-06-13}}</ref>

On November 25, 2008, Memphis assigned Haddadi to the [[Dakota Wizards]] of the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]]. On Tuesday, December 23, 2008, Haddadi was recalled by the Grizzlies.<ref name="dleague">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_assign_hamed_haddadi-to-dleague-081125.html?rss=true |title=Grizzlies assign Hamed Haddadi to NBA Development League's Dakota Wizards |work=Nba.com |access-date=2014-06-13}}</ref>  Haddadi scored a then career-high 10 points, with 8 rebounds and a block in less than 10 minutes to key a 12–0 run in the 4th quarter, sparking the Grizzlies to a come-from-behind victory at the [[Golden State Warriors]] on March 30, 2009.<ref>{{cite web|last=Tillery |first=Ronald |url=http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2009/mar/31/grizzlies-rally-beat-golden-state-warriors-114-109/ |title=Grizzlies rally to beat Golden State Warriors, 114–109 |publisher=Commercialappeal.com |access-date=2014-06-13}}</ref>

On December 31, 2011, he re-signed with the Memphis Grizzlies a one-year $1.3 million contract.<ref>{{cite web | title = Grizzlies sign Hamed Haddadi | url = http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-haddadi_signed-111230 | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2011-12-31 | access-date = 2012-01-01}}</ref> On April 17, 2012, Hamed came off the bench to score 8 points in 12 minutes and give the Grizzlies a boost to lead them to a victory over the rival Minnesota Timberwolves. On July 28, 2012, Haddadi re-signed with the Memphis Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web | title = Grizzlies re-sign Hamed Haddadi | url = http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/hamed_haddadi_resigned-120728 | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2012-07-28 | access-date = 2012-07-30}}</ref>

On January 30, 2013, Haddadi was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] along with [[Rudy Gay]] as part of a three-way deal that sent [[José Calderón (basketball)|José Calderón]] to the Detroit Pistons and [[Ed Davis (basketball)|Ed Davis]], [[Tayshaun Prince]], [[Austin Daye]], and a second round pick to the Memphis Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/01/30/aldridge-gaye-raptors-trade/index.html|title=Grizzlies deal Gay to Raptors in three-team trade|work=NBA.com|date=January 30, 2013|access-date=January 31, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130201091837/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/01/30/aldridge-gaye-raptors-trade/index.html|archive-date=February 1, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> However, Haddadi could not immediately report to the Raptors due to immigration issues.<ref>{{cite news|url= https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/2013/01/30/toronto_raptors_to_trade_jose_calderon_ed_davis_to_grizzlies_for_rudy_gay_reports.html|title=Toronto Raptors trade Jose Calderon, Ed Davis to Memphis Grizzlies for Rudy Gay|work=TheStar.com|date=January 30, 2013}}</ref>  He would never play a single game for the Raptors.

====Phoenix Suns====
On February 21, 2013, the Raptors traded Haddadi and a second-round draft pick to the [[Phoenix Suns]] for [[Sebastian Telfair]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Suns Acquire Haddadi, Second-Round Pick | url = http://www.nba.com/suns/suns-acquire-haddadi-second-round-pick | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2013-02-21 | access-date = 2013-02-22}}</ref> During his tenure with the Suns, Haddadi decided to wear the number 98 as a tribute of sorts to his home nation's national telephone code.<ref>{{cite web|last=Dwyer |first=Kelly |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/hamed-haddadi-phoenix-suns-jersey-iran-international-telephone-190021735--nba.html |title=Hamed Haddadi's new Phoenix Suns jersey is Iran's international telephone code (PHOTO) | Ball Don't Lie – Yahoo Sports |publisher=Sports.yahoo.com |date=2013-02-26 |access-date=2014-06-13}}</ref>

Haddadi did not play for the Suns until March 6, 2013, in a game against the Raptors, the team that Haddadi was first traded to. On March 9, 2013, Haddadi recorded 6 points, 3 blocks and a career-high 11 rebounds in 28 minutes off the bench, contributing to the Suns 107–105 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

Despite gaining professional career highs in his short stint with the team, Haddadi was waived by the Suns on June 29, 2013.<ref>{{cite web |last=Zimmerman |first=Kevin |url=http://valleyofthesuns.com/2013/06/29/shannon-brown-remains-with-suns-hamed-haddadi-waived/ |title=Shannon Brown remains with Suns, Hamed Haddadi waived |publisher=Valleyofthesuns.com |date=2013-06-29 |access-date=2014-06-13 |archive-date=2014-02-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140209140420/http://valleyofthesuns.com/2013/06/29/shannon-brown-remains-with-suns-hamed-haddadi-waived/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===China===
In September 2013, Haddadi signed with the [[Sichuan Blue Whales]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] as the bonus foreign Asian player that's allowed to be on the expansion CBA team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/world/asia/64094/hamed-haddadi-signs-in-china-with-sichuan.html |title=Hamed Haddadi signs in China with Sichuan |publisher=Sportando.net |date=2013-09-27 |access-date=2014-06-13}}</ref>

On September 15, 2014, Haddadi agreed to terms with [[Qingdao DoubleStar|Qingdao DoubleStar Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Qingdao Double Star agreed to terms with Hamed Haddadi |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/134715/qingdao-double-star-agreed-to-terms-with-hamed-haddadi.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304124403/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/134715/qingdao-double-star-agreed-to-terms-with-hamed-haddadi.html |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |access-date=2025-03-28 |work=Sportando |url-status=live }}</ref> With Haddadi's help, the Eagles were one of the top teams during the [[2014–15 CBA season|2014–15 season]]. During his time in Qingdao, Haddadi would average 20.4 points, 13.9 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 2.3 blocks for the team's surprise rise.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

In September 2015, Haddadi returned to the Sichuan Blue Whales as their bonus foreign Asian player due to them having one of the worst records that season. During his second stint in Sichuan, Haddadi would help the team reach their first playoff stint in CBA history. He would help the Blue Whales sweep the [[Zhejiang Lions]] in the first round and the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] in the second round before playing in the championship series against the [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]]. Before Haddadi would return to his home nation with [[Petrochimi Bandar Imam BC|Petrochimi Bandar Imam]] in Iran, he would help lead Sichuan to a 4–1 Finals series win over the [[Liaoning Flying Leopards]], and thus becoming the [[CBA Finals MVP]] in the process. After finishing his most recent stint in his home nation, he'd return to Sichuan as an exception player for the two international players allowed on their roster.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

After taking a year off from Chinese basketball, Haddadi returned to the CBA once again, this time playing as a starting centre for the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

==National team career==
[[File:PZK 20140803 Toruń Basket Cup 5968.jpg|thumbnail|Haddadi with the national team in 2014.]]
Haddadi won a silver medal at the [[Asian Basketball Confederation Under-18 Championship 2002|2002 Asian Under-18 Championship]] and a gold medal at the [[Asian Basketball Confederation Under-20 Championship 2004|2004 Asian U20 Championship]] while playing on Iran's junior national teams. He won gold medals at the 2004 and 2005 West Asian Championships with the senior [[Iran national basketball team|Iranian national basketball team]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

Haddadi also won a bronze medal at the [[Basketball at the 2006 Asian Games|2006 Asian Games]] and gold medals at the [[2007 FIBA Asia Championship]], [[2009 FIBA Asia Championship]], and the [[2013 FIBA Asia Championship]]. He was also named the [[FIBA Asia Cup MVP|MVP of the latter four tournaments]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

At the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics|2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing]], he led the tournament with the highest average blocked shots per game and rebounds per game.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

Haddadi was involved in a brawl in the 2009 William Jones cup against team Jordan, which was a vital game in the cup. It later led to the outcome of the championship where Iran won despite having a 6–2 standing while Jordan had a 7–1 record.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

Haddadi led team Iran to back-to-back FIBA Asia championships, where they beat Jordan in the semifinals 77–75, and defeated tournament favorite and host China, 70–52.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

Haddadi scored a game high 18 points in a loss to [[France men's national basketball team|France]] in the preliminary round of the [[2020 Summer Olympics|2020 Olympics]] in Tokyo.

===Retired Number===
The [[Islamic Republic of Iran Basketball Federation|Iran Basketball Federation]] retired Hamed Haddadi's '''number 15''' jersey on 21 February 2025, ahead of an Asia cup Qualifying game against India. It was the first jersey number retirement in [[Iran]] for any sport.

==Other ventures==
In September 2009, Haddadi hosted a weekend basketball camp for children on the campus of [[California State University, Northridge]]. The camp catered mainly to the [[Iranian American]] community, and coaches included Haddadi himself, his manager, Mayar Zokaei, [[Los Angeles Lakers]] forward [[Metta Sandiford-Artest|Ron Artest]] (now known as Metta World Peace), and Iranian professional basketball players [[Behdad Sami]] and Benny Koochoie, amongst others. The camp attracted over 100 children and was the first sports camp ever by an Iranian athlete in the United States.<ref name=camp>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2009/news/features/09/14/haddadi.camp/ |title=Haddadi camps brings hoops to Iranian-American community |work=Nba.com |date=2009-09-14 |access-date=2014-06-13 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140927063807/http://www.nba.com/2009/news/features/09/14/haddadi.camp/ |archive-date=2014-09-27 }}</ref>

Haddadi also spearheaded the ''Hamed Haddadi Javanan Foundation'', a charity organization formed with the intention of awarding college scholarships to student athletes across the nation.<ref name=camp/>
